x: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Commentary on Sūrat "al-Qadr"
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:
h

Indeed We sent it down on the Night of al-Qadr (1) And what will make you know what the Night of al-Qadr is? (2) The Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months (3) The angels and the Spirit descend in it by the permission of their Lord, with every command (4) Peace it is until the rising of dawn (5)
He, exalted be His mention, says: We sent down this Qurʾān all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of al-Qadr, which is the night of judgment, in which God decrees the decree of the year.

The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of this.

The Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months

c: Salm b. Qutayba told us, he said: al-Qāsim b. al-Faḍl told us, from ʿĪsā b.
m: Māzin, he said: I said to al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī ؓ: "O you who have blackened the faces of the believers, you proceeded (3) to this man and pledged allegiance to him!" meaning Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān. He said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ was shown in his sleep the Umayyads ascending his pulpit, caliph after caliph, and that distressed him. So God sent down:
Indeed We have granted you al-Kawthar
Indeed We sent it down on the Night of al-Qadr (1) And what will make you know what the Night of al-Qadr is? (2) The Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months

": meaning the kingdom of the Umayyads. al-Qāsim said: "We reckoned the kingdom of the Umayyads, and it was a thousand months" (1). The most similar of these views to the apparent sense of the revelation is the view of those who said: deeds on the Night of al-Qadr are better than the deeds of a thousand months in which there is no Night of al-Qadr. As for the other views, they are claims of meanings (2) that are false, for which there is no evidence from a report or from reason, nor are they found in the revelation.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of His saying {until the rising of dawn}.

The general body of the reciters of the regions, except Yaḥyā b. Wathāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī, read {*maṭlaʿi* al-fajr} with a *fatḥa* on the *lām* (3), in the sense of: until the rising (*ṭulūʿ*) of dawn.

The correct reading in our view is the *fatḥa* on the *lām* (1), because its meaning is sound in Arabic: *maṭlaʿ* with a *fatḥa* is the rising, whereas *maṭliʿ* with a *kasra* is the place from which something rises, and there is no sense in the place of rising in this context.
